docs.purpose: Lets a user who deleted their account within the last 30 days restore it, giving back exactly the access their real current subscription status supports for each product — rather than assuming they are still subscribed.
docs.data_story: It reads 2 tables — `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes `entitlements` and `user_profiles`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 28 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `shell_app_root`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Also cites docs/specs/00-architecture/116_multi_product_architecture.md §4. Blocks reactivation after the 30-day window. For non-manufacturer accounts it calls Stripe subscriptions.list and derives real per-product status via deriveEffectiveStripeStatusByProduct in src/lib/stripe/client.ts, which itself reads logic_variables through resolvePriceProduct; a Stripe outage is loud-non-fatal and falls back to the 'expired' catch-all. Response uses the same CLIENT_SAFE_JOINED_SELECT whitelist as GET /api/user-profile (src/lib/userProfile.schema.ts) so no internal or PII columns leak. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: The Stripe read is LOUD-NON-FATAL: a throw is caught at :102-107 and restoredByProduct is reset to an empty Map, so every product falls through to the 'expired' catch-all (:151-156) and the account is still restored — a 200 here does not prove the live subscription status was consulted. `last_stripe_event_at = NOW()` is re-stamped (not cleared) on every touched row (:140, :153) — the rationale at :117-129 is that NULL would disable the webhook's out-of-order watermark (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:171). The logic_variables read is INDIRECT (route -> deriveEffectiveStripeStatusByProduct -> resolvePriceProduct), which is why it is easy to miss. CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches (reads user_profiles + logic_variables; writes entitlements + user_profiles) — the census read list omits entitlements, which IS read via the LEFT JOIN at :24/:168. | Idempotency: Effectively guarded by state: after a successful call account_deleted_at is NULL, so a replay falls into the NOT_DELETED 400 at :54-59 and writes nothing. Within one call, every entitlement write is an absolute assignment inside a single transaction with the user_profiles UPDATE (:130-170); the catch-all is predicate-scoped to rows still in 'cancelled_pending_deletion' (:154) so ordering is safe. NOTE: the Stripe read happens BEFORE the transaction (:93-108, deliberate per the comment at :89-90), so a concurrent subscription change between the read and the write is not serialised. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-180) | Entitlement posture: No entitlement gate on entry; the route WRITES entitlement statuses. State gates instead: the profile must be in a deleted state (account_deleted_at non-null, :54-59) and within the 30-day recovery window (:61-68). A non-UUID uid skips every entitlement write (:133, guard defined src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:70-75). | Locking tests: src/tests/reactivate-stripe.infra.test.ts, src/tests/user-profiles.infra.test.ts.
